answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable bond before it may claim rewards, with payouts released only after peers verify completed work. A ridge of independent attestations makes one operator’s copied identities poor substitutes for trusted agents: each new identity needs its own bond and must earn credibility through costly participation. The pearl is that reputation cannot be bought instantly; a detected fraud burns the bond and triggers a ripple of lost standing across linked accounts.
